problem: A metal plate occupies the region $D={(x,y):-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le x\le {y}^{2}}.$ The charge density of the plate is given by $\rho (x,y)=x{y}^{2}.$ Find the total charge $Q$ of the plate.
worked_solution:
The total charge $Q$ of a plate that occupies the region $D$ with charge density $\rho (x,y)=x{y}^{2}$ is given by

$$
Q={∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066271/assets/1cbe96aa4bf517302a2329db9f8eb2e9c56873e4d5a18cd5f1cd676543e97086.png)

Notice that $D$ is a type II region. So, we can express the integral as follows:

$$
{∬}_{D}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}A={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}x{y}^{2}\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y
$$

First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $x$, treating $y$ as a constant:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}[{\int }_{0}^{{y}^{2}}x\,\text{d}x]\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}{[\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{{y}^{2}}\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{2}(\frac{{y}^{4}}{2}-0)\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we integrate with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{-1}^{1}{y}^{6}\,\text{d}y & =\frac{1}{2}{[\frac{{y}^{7}}{7}]}_{-1}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{{1}^{7}}{7}-(-\frac{{1}^{7}}{7})) \\  & =\frac{1}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the total charge of the plate is $Q=\frac{1}{7}.$
